claims.text: Large language models are prone to hallucination, generating plausible yet nonfactual content.
LLM hallucinations present distinct challenges that diverge from prior task-specific models due to open-ended general-purpose attributes inherent to LLMs.
Retrieval-augmented LLMs face limitations in combating hallucinations within information retrieval systems.

evidence.description: LLMs are prone to hallucination, generating plausible yet nonfactual content.
Given the open-ended general-purpose attributes inherent to LLMs, LLM hallucinations present distinct challenges that diverge from prior task-specific models.
Additionally, we delve into the current limitations faced by retrieval-augmented LLMs in combating hallucinations, offering insights for developing more robust IR systems.

methodologies.name: Literature Survey and Taxonomy Framework
methodologies.description: A structured review and taxonomy categorizing LLM hallucinations, contributing factors, detection methods, benchmarks, and mitigation strategies.

limitations.text: Retrieval-augmented LLMs face limitations in combating hallucinations when deployed in information retrieval systems.

future_work.text: Investigating hallucinations in large vision-language models.
Understanding knowledge boundaries in LLM hallucinations.
